data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The fetch budget should be denominated in wall-clock time, with exhaustion recorded as a typed terminal event containing the elapsed time and time limit, and the agent's fetch operations are time-budgeted using a deterministic virtual clock to ensure replayability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"This approach is complex and requires careful calibration of time costs.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"It may not map well to real-world costs where time is not the only resource.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent's processing time between fetches is significant, that would need to be accounted for, adding complexity.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"SRC_003 critiques wall-clock time as violating replayability; this candidate addresses that by using a virtual clock, but the virtual clock parameters must be fixed and auditable.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Instead of requests or bytes, the budget is a time limit. The agent has a virtual clock that advances by a fixed amount per fetch (e.g., 1 second per request) plus an amount proportional to bytes transferred (e.g., 1 second per 1MB). This combines both dimensions into a single time-based metric. Exhaustion occurs when the virtual clock exceeds the limit. The virtual clock is deterministic, so replayability is preserved.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
